pr_title: Set settings section as selected if user presses the sidebar button
pr_body:
Closes #9196

![settings](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11320483/100555208-8b69f580-32a2-11eb-8098-479e3539b8b7.gif)

~~I assume the section we scroll to has to reach the search box to be considered selected but currently it will never reach that (at least not high enough to always satisfy ``<= 0``)~~

~~Considering the margin when deciding what section is selected sounds most reasonable, but maybe this should be even more than ``51`` because users would consider the section reached well before.~~
pr_comments:
I don't think this is a correct solution. This is actually an issue with the comparison-to-zero which suffers from floating-point precision issues. I'm claiming that based on the following log excerpt I acquired when I logged what the `diff` function returns for each section when navigating between them:

Note that at the first click, the diff value never satisfies `<= 0`, and then begins to oscillate on subsequent clicks. Each button actually behaves slightly differently (some of them will reach 0, but only after an inordinately long wait).

I get that it's a floating-point precision issue, but I also think the section should be considered reached well before the diff satisfies ``<= 0``. ``Margin.Top`` (or ``51`` which it equals to) starts to sound more and more like an arbitrary number in my head, maybe something more like 1/4th the overlay height would be a better number to use.
all of these sound more arbitrary to me than 0 if I'm honest.

I'm suggesting something way bigger than 0 because I think users would consider the "Skin" section reached on this screenshot and would find it weird that the button isn't highlighted.
![osu_2020-11-29_22-14-42](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11320483/100552517-58b70180-3290-11eb-85a5-90b762b62029.png)

I don't think something like some % of container height is arbitrary for this.

then why isn't "input" reached? if we're going that far, then surely all sections which have a part of them visible on the screen should be highlighted, no?

(side note, just noticed that the positioning of the "seasonal backgrounds" options makes zero sense. it's in audio settings.)

> then surely all sections which have a part of them visible on the screen should be highlighted

#9594 ?

well if that was rejected, then i'd say it should either be reaching the search box as is currently, or an entirely different measure of determining selection should be used (i.e. the section which has most of it visible on screen at the current moment is selected). that's way less arbitrary than saying "the section is selected when you cross the top 25% of the screen", because that arbitrary percentage has no visible reference point.

If you're going to go in this direction and remove the animation during scroll (i think it feels okay without it so i'm neutral), why not fix it in a permanent way - match on the last clicked section rather than Y coordinates.

Your change doesn't fix all cases, see this scenario:

![2020-11-30 18 32 11](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/100592446-7640a580-333a-11eb-9433-9650a82170e4.gif)

I think I'll try to implement what bdach suggested, as in have the section which takes up the most of visible area consider as selected, and see how that looks. Something like that should look better, fix the issue, keep the animation, and would not introduce a new class.

Closing in favour of #11019

Added ``UserTrackingScrollContainer`` in there instead, but with more sound logic for the very last item.

issue_context.title: Settings menu button click not highlighted correctly
issue_context.body:
![osu_2020-06-03_10-56-32](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48766178/83617127-eedfc880-a588-11ea-9297-2d8d50396772.jpg)

When clicking a section button in the settings menu, the game scrolls to the section, but the button is not highlighted. When changing the ScrollTo definition in SectionsContainer.cs to
`public void ScrollTo(Drawable section) =>
            scrollContainer.ScrollTo(scrollContainer.GetChildPosInContent(section) - (FixedHeader?.BoundingBox.Height ?? 0), false);
` 
to disable the animation of the scroll, the problem doesn't occur, implying that somewhere in the scrollTo definition of the framework (probably, I cant find it), UpdateAfterChildren is run before the scroll animation ends, which causes the Update to highlight the section before the correct
